publicationCopy.title: Build Your Perfect Chest Workout
publicationCopy.caption:
Flat presses, incline presses, decline presses, and flyes. Compare two options in each group and choose what fits your gym and your training.

Save this for your next chest day.

reference.author: robinbaumann
reference.used: Exercise names paired with short setup cues, rather than a bare list.
reference.rejected: Inner-chest isolation, guaranteed best hypertrophy, and dumbbell low-to-high fly claims.

reference.author: demicstory
reference.rejected: Every-area targeting as a literal anatomical guarantee.

sources.use: Flat, incline and decline are exercise-selection categories; regional emphasis is not isolation. Acute EMG does not prove a hypertrophy ranking.
Barbell and dumbbell press variants at flat, incline and decline angles were directly compared. No exclusive regional growth or optimal ranking claims are made.
Pec deck and cable fly exercise selection; no acute activation ranking is adopted.

slides.name: Choose Your Chest Exercises
text: Pick the moves that work for you

slides.name: Chest Presses
text:
Keep your shoulder blades
back against the bench.

Keep your wrists stacked
above your elbows.

slides.name: Upper Chest
text:
Start with a low incline
that feels comfortable.

Set the bench so the bar
lowers to your upper chest.

slides.name: Lower Chest
text:
Hook your feet under the pads.
Don't bounce the bar.

Don't bang the dumbbells
together at the top.

slides.name: Chest Flyes
text:
Keep your back on the pad
throughout each rep.

Bend your elbows slightly.
Keep your torso still.
